correctness.rationale: For n=1 the graph is K_m and a nonempty dominating set must leave at most k vertices out. For n≥2, the word rule gives at most one link per vertex, tied to the symbol preceding its maximal constant suffix, and exactly one link per adjacent pair of quotient prefixes. The omitted-set relation has k residues per row (the symmetric ± offsets, plus a common diagonal bit if k is odd) with no duplicate offsets because 2 floor(k/2)≤m−1. The last two symbols of linked words are either transposes or both diagonal, so no link crosses membership. Every row clique has m−k selected vertices; domination and the limitedness bound follow inside each row. For the lower bound a nonempty row requires at least m−k selections; an empty row forces every linked endpoint on the other side to be selected and gives each neighboring row at least m−k+1 selections. In a quotient clique of size m at most one row can be empty, and then (m−1)(m−k+1)=m(m−k)+(k−1). Summation proves equality for all stated parameters. I independently reconstructed word adjacencies and checked constructions on nine instances and all smaller subsets on six of them, including S(2,4) for every k; replay: python3 /workspace/checks/frozen_review_checks.py sierpinski. The proof, not these tests, establishes the universal claim.
